evidence: Plan item 2.5 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md): the Displacement Directions page opened at nu = 10 with 2 smoothing passes, while analyze_displacement_directions lets the engine choose the tiling (recommendedFrequency: the finest nu whose cells still average at least 12 displacements) and never smooths, so a user, arm A and the Copilot read one site on two tilings: on dev-thermal-null's three flattened O sites (512 copies) the map test read 2.32, 2.16 and 2.23 sigma on the page against 7.17, 6.30 and 7.13 sigma on the tool (nu = 2). Every number the page shows or arm A reads, checked against the smoothing: the map test, the +u/-u asymmetry and its null, the Bingham anisotropy, and the hover's counts and local z come from the raw counts or the vectors and do not move with it; but both engines pick the peak cell on the smoothed enhancement, so the peak's cell, direction, enhancement, tie count and sigma did (the test applies the picked cell's raw count, conservative whichever cell is picked, but not the tool's cell). At the old default (nu = 10, 2 passes against 0) dev-zone-boundary's O site 5 read -10.4 against -0.28 sigma (the smoothed peak cell held 2 raw atoms, the fullest 4) and dev-offcentre's K site 1 -5.63 against -3.06 sigma in another direction; on the engine's own tiling with 2 passes dev-thermal-null's Ti read -2.06 against -0.69 sigma at a direction 90 deg away, dev-offcentre's K -2.88 against -1.33 sigma with x and y reversed, and a judgment case's split site put its peak in the antipodal cell. The colorbar's maximum and the hover's enhancement and mean |dr| describe the drawn map and stay smoothed with it. The change: the page opens at Auto, the engine's resolution, with the nu it chose in the Auto choice's label; every readout is the raw histogram's at the page's analysis settings (smoothing 0, the tool's request); the map is the same request smoothed; arm A reads the page's own defaults (src/directionSettings.js). Known answer (validation/__tests__/directionsDefault.test.js): on every site of dev-thermal-null the page's default readout equals the tool's result field for field and arm A's reading equals the tool's numbers; the O sites clear 3 sigma on the map test and were below it on the old default; with 2 passes the counts, map, asymmetry and Bingham tests are unchanged and the peak cell moves on at least one site. Arms A and A+ on the dev set before and after: every D record identical, and every score of the ten paired cases; nine records move, each through a split site's Displacement Directions reading, which now records the nu it read. dev-offcentre A and A+: Nb 4.33 -> 17.2 sigma at nu = 2, the claim's direction [0.1 0.06 -1] -> [0 0 -1] (within tolerance before and after). dev-zone-boundary A: Ti 2.29 -> 5.44 sigma, now significant, so the spurious off_centre Ti names the peak [0 0 1] instead of PC1's [-0.03 0.1 1]; the same score. dev-jahn-teller A and A+: F 2.71 -> 6.58 sigma at nu = 1, the tolerated off_centre F names the coarse peak [-1 0 -0.62] instead of PC1's [1 0 -0.01]; the same scores. Two judgment cases move in A and A+ (their values in validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json and the arms.test.js pins): on dev-jt-off-centre a split site small enough for Auto's nu = 1 (twelve cells whose centres lie 31.7 deg from every cube axis, so an axial lobe falls on a cell boundary) now reads a significant peak 31.7 deg off its planted axis, beyond the 15 deg tolerance, and its off-centre direction scores off in both arms, a side miss beside the case's situation; on dev-octahedral-clusters the tolerated claim names the other end of the same axis. The dev thermal case's own records do not move: the arms read the direction map of split sites only, and it has none. The test set was not run. The model-visible snapshots pass unchanged: the tool, its result and what the model sees are unchanged. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: The page and the tool at the same settings: the Displacement Directions page opens at Auto, the engine's recommended frequency (the tiling analyze_displacement_directions reads), and labels the Auto choice with the nu it chose for the site on screen; a picked resolution overrides it and stays as every option on the page does (page state: kept across a site change, a tab switch and another run; a Copilot step's Show in still sets it). Every readout under the sphere comes from the raw histogram at the page's analysis settings (smoothing 0); the sphere, its colorbar and the hover draw the same request smoothed, so smoothing stays a display setting. One module holds the defaults and both requests (src/directionSettings.js; src/useDirectionHistogram.js asks for both, and only for the map on a smoothing change); arm A, and A+ through the same reading, reads the page's defaults from it (ARM_A_RULES.DIRECTION_SETTINGS is DIRECTION_DEFAULTS); PROTOCOL_VERSION 2026-10-19.16; the moved dev records re-recorded in validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json, the others as recorded. The tool and the engines are unchanged. Left open for the user: a tiling names a direction only to within its cell (up to 37 deg at nu = 1), and arm A's rule takes a significant peak's direction over PC1's; the displacement-anisotropy skill still says the page defaults to nu = 10, smoothed (SKILL.md lines 49 and 74-75), for the user's skill review (the skills are what the model reads, so not edited here). Commit bc30982. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
